title: Maximum Coins From K Consecutive Bags
summary: Given an infinite line of bags, each containing a certain number of coins within specified segments, determine the maximum number of coins that can be collected from any k consecutive bags.
statement: Given an infinite line of bags, each containing a certain number of coins within specified segments, determine the maximum number of coins that can be collected from any k consecutive bags.
constraints: coins contains up to 100,000 pairwise non-overlapping inclusive segments [left,right,value].
Every bag in a segment holds value coins and bags outside all segments hold zero.
Return the maximum coins in any k consecutive integer positions.
hints: An optimal window can slide until its left edge meets a segment start or its right edge meets a segment end.
Build a prefix integral over sorted weighted segments and evaluate both endpoint-derived starts.
Use binary search to compute coins through any coordinate; subtract prefix values for each candidate length-k window.
Between segment boundaries the window total changes linearly, so a maximum occurs at one of the evaluated boundary events.
editorial: Between segment boundaries the window total changes linearly, so a maximum occurs at one of the evaluated boundary events.

tests.explanation: The four bags from three through six collect two plus zero plus four plus four, totaling ten.
A length-five window can cover the whole segment, collecting six coins.
